<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b920f6dd09690d88107db420f2c54fd1f2b5363` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `1d844ba0125b74bd5e061f6c87291f5c9a36c23e` — the merge of head `12e4f3495ae6a547dc3be726178493b53c54cb97` into base `3b920f6dd09690d88107db420f2c54fd1f2b5363`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `12e4f3495ae6a547dc3be726178493b53c54cb97`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-connections.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/oauth2-grant/grant-handle.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/oauth2-grant/token-endpoint.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-connector-connection.object.ts, content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published surface — right.** The diff moves one JSDoc bullet on `ConnectorConnectionState.status` (L1134–1142 at the head). No type, member, export or value changes: `status` stays `'not_connected' | 'connected' | 'reconnect_required'`, `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` record names only and are untouched. The text ships in the `.d.ts` of `@objectstack/spec/contracts`, so the package publishes new bytes.
- **Generated artifacts — right, nothing to regenerate.** `contracts/` holds TypeScript interfaces, not `.zod.ts` schemas; `gen:schema` leaves `json-schema/contracts/` empty and `build-docs.ts` emits no page for it (`scripts/build-docs.ts` L918–924), so neither `check:docs` nor `check:authorable-surface` carries this description. `Lint & Repo Gates` (which runs `check:generated`, `check:api-surface`) is `success` on the head; `Spec property liveness` is `success`.
- **Writers of `reconnect_required`, counted on the head tree — the bullet is complete and names nothing the code does not do.** Exactly one store write: `connector-connections.ts` L331–341 `markReconnectRequired` (`status: 'reconnect_required', status_reason: reason, refresh_token: null`, conditional on the row's revision). Two callers:
  1. `grant-handle.ts` L214–226 `grantRefused`, reached from `refreshOnce` three ways — L267–270 `resolveRefreshToken` answers nothing ("issued no refresh token, so an expired access token cannot be renewed"); L271–275 `endpointOf` returns `undefined` ("keeps no client to refresh it with"); L283 the token endpoint throws `OAuth2GrantRefusedError`, which `token-endpoint.ts` L90–99 raises for `invalid_grant` only (`invalid_client` / `unauthorized_client` is `OAuth2ClientRefusedError`, never routed to `grantRefused`, so it does not mark the row — the bullet rightly does not claim it).
  2. `plugin.ts` L3306–3317 → L3724–3747 `holdConnectorForRefusedConnection`, taken only when `isConnectorCredentialRejected(thrown) && discoveryConnection !== undefined`; `discoveryConnection` is set at L3195–3203 only for `provider === 'mcp'` with an `authorization_code` grant. The `mcp` provider throws `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError` for a borrowed token only on the SDK's HTTP 401/403 at connect, handshake or `tools/list` (`mcp-provider.ts` L472–497, `credentialRejectionStatus`); the `include`-missing 403 path (L561) needs `credentialSent`, which is false for an `oauth2` instance because its `ctx.auth` is `undefined` (`plugin.ts` L3251–3253; `ResolvedConnectorAuth` excludes `oauth2`, `connector-auth.zod.ts` L135–138). So "the upstream refused the connection's token while an `mcp` instance discovered its tools" is exactly the fourth trigger, and the `mcp` qualifier is correct.
- **Readers — consistent.** `plugin.ts` L3967–3978 `describeConnection` serves `record.status` and `statusReason` unchanged; `grant-handle.ts` L209 and L260 refuse a dispatch on the status; `plugin.ts` L2938–2949 holds the instance with the first row's `statusReason`; the Console (`ConnectorConnectionsPage.tsx` L215–219) labels it "Reconnect required". None of them depends on the old single-cause reading.
- **Docs drift — nothing to list** (check `Flag docs affected by code changes` `success`; the drift bot found no page naming the anchor). One hand-written restatement of the old single cause exists outside this PR: `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` L689–691 ("When the vendor refuses the grant (`invalid_grant`), the connection is marked **reconnect required**") and L868. Out of this card's file surface; named in ③.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28614-connection-reconnect-required-docblock.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, body carries `Clause-②: no` (no arm) and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two line-initial declarations. **Right.** AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist 3: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`; `skip-changeset` is only for a diff that publishes nothing from a released package, and this JSDoc ships in the published `.d.ts`. No metadata author can write anything differently (`ConnectorConnectionState` is a service answer, not authorable metadata), so `none` is the right kind. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head. The changeset format matches the sibling `.changeset/26702-mcp-discovery-refusal-marks-connection.md`.
- `Clause-②: no` — right: no declared capability is added, widened or taken away at any consumer; the three-literal union is unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 — `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (full build prerequisite): **answered** by `Lint & Repo Gates` `success` on `12e4f349`.
- Dev deviation 2 — the bullet names a third trigger (no refresh token / no client) beyond the card's "Wanted" two: **answered, right.** Measured above at `grant-handle.ts` L267–275; the card's "Wanted" is "in substance", and a docblock that named two of four writers would restate the defect it fixes.
- Dev `open_questions`: `[]`. Nothing to escalate.
- Dev out-of-scope findings (the `sys_connector_connection` `status` description at `sys-connector-connection.object.ts` L98, `markReconnectRequired`'s docblock at `connector-connections.ts` L325–330, and `reconnectRequiredReason`'s opening clause at `grant-handle.ts` L122–126 reused on paths where no server was asked): confirmed in the tree; filed by the seat as #28863 (open, `finding`). Not this PR's surface; nothing more owed here.
- **New, for triage to route (not a must-fix on this card):** `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` L689–691 and L868 still give `invalid_grant` as the only cause of "reconnect required"; the drift check cannot see it (no shared anchor). Fits #28863's dedupe words (`reconnect_required`) — triage may fold it there.
- Check-runs on the head at reading: 24 `success`, 13 `skipped` (opt-in / path-filtered), 0 failed, **29 `in_progress`**: `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Test UI (1–16/16)`, `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. Stated pending, not assumed green; landing waits for them. Every lint, changeset, api-surface, liveness, governed-queue and PR-body gate is already green.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` — judged against the ruling it implements (ADR-0143 D4 as carried by PR #28598's Acceptance notes and the reading 6553121554 on #26702), its first consumer (`plugin.ts` `describeConnection`, served through the connection door and the Console), and every writer of the value on the head tree.

- "the grant stopped working" — holds; it is the same phrase `statusReason`'s own docblock already uses (L1144), so the two members now read as one.
- "the authorization server refused it on refresh" — holds (`grant-handle.ts` L283, `invalid_grant` only). A refresh is also where the client refusal and an unreachable endpoint surface, and neither marks the row (`OAuth2ClientRefusedError` / `ConnectorUpstreamUnavailableError` propagate past `grantRefused`); the bullet rightly stays silent on them.
- "the connection keeps nothing to renew an expired access token with (no refresh token was issued, or no client to refresh with)" — the two parentheticals are exactly the two `grantRefused` entries at L267–275. **Should-fix (non-blocking):** "expired" is narrower than the code. `get()` refreshes on any cache miss (L333–337: a replica that never seeded the token, or a `revision` moved by another replica) and `refresh()` on a dispatch's 401, so a connection with no refresh token is marked on the first dispatch from a fresh replica even while its access token is still valid. "an access token it has to renew" would be exact. The runtime's own appended sentence (L268–269) uses the same "expired", so the spec and the stored `statusReason` agree with each other today; fixing one without the other would make them disagree, which is why this is a should-fix routed with #28863, not a must-fix here.
- "or the upstream refused the connection's token while an `mcp` instance discovered its tools" — holds and is exactly scoped (① above: `mcp` only, 401/403 on the borrowed token only, not the `include`-missing path). The guard that marks only while the row is still the same connect (`plugin.ts` L3744) is a write-safety detail, not a meaning the status carries; omitting it is right.
- "`statusReason` says which." — holds: the four writers pass four distinct platform sentences (`reconnectRequiredReason` bare, plus two appended causes; `discoveryTokenRefusedReason` naming the HTTP status), and `describeConnection` serves the row's text verbatim. The shared misleading opening clause on the two no-server paths is #28863's.
- Tried to break it: searched the head for any other write of `status: 'reconnect_required'` or `status_reason` on `sys_connector_connection` (none besides `markReconnectRequired`; `recordRefresh`/connect write `status_reason: null` at L254), any non-`mcp` provider reaching `holdConnectorForRefusedConnection` (impossible, `discoveryConnection` is `mcp`-gated), and any `toRecord` mapping that could surface the value from another column (L80 maps only the literal). Nothing the bullet omits; nothing it invents.
- Card's ask met: both "Wanted" causes are present, `statusReason` is pointed to, and the one extra cause is measured, not asserted. No must-fix.
